newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan's 1Q '97 oil imports tender under review.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's 1Q '97 oil imports tender under review.

text.p: A decision on issuing Pakistan's oil products purchase tender for the first quarter of 1997 would be made late next week after the new oil minister has reviewed policy directions on imports, a government official said on Thursday.
"At the moment things are not clear," the official with the ministry of petroleum and natural resources told Reuters by telephone.
Benazir Bhutto and her government were sacked on Tuesday in a presidential decree.
"If all things go well a decision on whether or not a tender would be issued for first quarter 1997 would be known around November 15," the official said.
"The new oil minister and the secretary to the ministry will have to be briefed on current policies and they will have to decide whether or not new directions for imports have to be taken," he said.
The new petroleum and natural resources minister under the caretaker government has been named as Javed Jabbar, who replaces Anwar Saifullah.
The secretary to the ministry was named as Gulfaraz Ahmed, who took over from Syed Nasseer Ahmad, the official said.
President Farooq Leghari appointed Meraj Khalid as interim Prime Minister on November 5 after dismissing Bhutto and her cabinet. Several new ministers have been sworn in since.
The interim prime minister has to hold general elections within 90 days by around February 3 by which time a new oil minister might be appointed.

The official said issues for review, included the country's import policy -- whether to continue with the current method of importing 75 percent of its oil products by term contracts and 25 percent by quarterly tenders, or to import 100 percent by term contracts.

But he said it was unlikely the interim oil minister would change the current import method because quarterly tenders allowed the ministry to keep track of price trends which was useful when negotiating annual term contracts.
Pakistan has term contracts with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) and Jeddah-based trader Bakri Trading.

In its last quarterly tender, for October-December deliveries, Pakistan bought 360,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel, 100,000 tonnes of 180-centistoke grade fuel oil and 200,000 tonnes of the 125-grade and up to 75,000 tonnes of 80-octane gasoline.
